newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tiasa says timber vendors agree on sale.
newsitem.headline: Tiasa says timber vendors agree on sale.

text.p: Malaysia's Jaya Tiasa Holdings Bhd said nine of 11 vendors of timber concessions which the company were planning to buy, have formally accepted a revised pricing scheme for the acquisitions.
The other two firms have given in-principle agreements to the revised conditions imposed by the Securities Commission, the company's merchant bankers said in a statement late on Monday.
Jaras Sdn Bhd and Lembaga Amanah Kebajikan Darul Falah, which have not formally accepted the revised proposals, together control 89,754 hectares of timber concessions valued at 36.3 million ringgit.
These represent 12.6 percent of the total timber concession area and 9.3 percent of the total valuation of the 11 concessions.
Timber products firm Jaya Tiasa last month said the commissions have approved the planned acquisitions and that of two other new timber licences at a revised price of 388.9 million ringgit.
The company had proposed to pay 576.1 million ringgit for the acquisitions.
Jaya Tiasa also requested the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange to requote its stock, which last traded on May 16 at 11.80.
